title: fix(plugin-auth)!: a user a SCIM directory provisions reads idp_provisioned from its creation, and earlier ones are marked once at boot
body:
Fixes #32113

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — every refusal keyed on a directory-owned identity (`sys_user.source = 'idp_provisioned'`) now applies to SCIM-provisioned users: `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager` answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with reason `idp_provisioned`, `admin/set-user-password` on a cloud-managed environment refuses them, and the self-service local-credential actions are hidden for them (ADR-0135 D4, D5.2).
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill or hand-written docs page states which identity source a SCIM-provisioned user reads; the generated SCIM reference is unchanged.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:SCIM 目录建出来的用户,从创建那一刻起就标记为目录托管(`idp_provisioned`);升级前已由目录建出的用户,在启动时按其 SCIM subject 记录一次性补标。
- 为什么改:ADR-0135 D4 要求目录托管的身份必须被标记,依赖这个标记的管理端拒绝(设经理、设密码)和自助入口隐藏才会对 SCIM 用户生效。
- 风险与回滚:管理员对 SCIM 用户"设经理"等操作会被拒(这是 BREAKING 收窄);持有本地密码的用户仍保持 `env_native`。回滚即 revert 本 PR;已写入的标记需要按需手工改回。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-identity-source.ts`(规则与补标)、`auth-manager.ts` 的 `reconcileScimUserLifecycle` 开头新增的标记调用、`auth-plugin.ts` 新增的 kernel:ready 补标钩子。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts`,预期 19/19 通过,其中 `(h)` 开头的 6 条是本次新增。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

ADR-0135 D4: a user a SCIM directory provisions is marked directory-managed (`sys_user.source = 'idp_provisioned'`) from the moment SCIM creates it, and users a directory provisioned earlier are marked once at boot.

- **The SCIM write path.** `@better-auth/scim` keeps its directory links in its own tables (`sys_scim_user`, `sys_scim_subject`). The seam every SCIM user write passes through is the vendor's `identity.reconcileUser` host callback (`AuthManager#reconcileScimUserLifecycle`): `POST /Users` calls it on a create, a link to an existing user, a tombstone re-link and the reprovision of an inactive source, and PUT, PATCH, DELETE and a projection-domain reconcile call it too. The callback now writes the mark first, through the data engine, which joins the vendor's SCIM transaction as its ambient transaction (`source` is not a vendor field, so the vendor adapter would drop it). The mark commits with the SCIM write; a mark that cannot be written fails the SCIM request, which the identity provider retries. The write carries the same connection attribution as every other write of the SCIM request.
- **The boot backfill.** A new `kernel:ready` pass in `auth-plugin.ts` marks every user that owns a `sys_scim_subject` row (the vendor creates one for every SCIM-provisioned user and never deletes it), keyset-paged through `keysetWalk`. It writes only a row whose value is wrong, so a second boot writes nothing, and it logs `marked N of M directory-provisioned user(s)` at `info`. An absent `sys_scim_subject` table reads as zero users; any other read failure is reported at `error` with the consequence and the remedy.
- **One rule, both callers** (`scim-identity-source.ts#markDirectoryProvisionedUsers`): a user already reading `idp_provisioned`, or holding a local password (`sys_account.provider_id = 'credential'`), is left as it is. That is the federated branch of `stampIdentitySource`, unchanged, so a SCIM user who later sets a local password keeps the `env_native` its credential branch flips them to, through later SCIM syncs and boots.
- The `sys_account` `afterInsert` stamp in `auth-plugin.ts` stays for adapter-level account creates; its comment and its two `error` lines no longer name SCIM as its path (`durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` follows the new wording).
- The tenant-audit write-call-site census is re-measured for the one new write site (301 sites, 208 decidable, 123 with run-time elevation); the census page's prose figures follow.

## Tests

- `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts`, new top-level describes `(h)`, all through the real vendor `POST /Users` on a real `ObjectQL` + better-sqlite3 engine:
  - `POST /Users marks the created user directory-managed, with no sys_account row to key on`
  - `POST /Users that re-links a deleted user through its tombstone marks that user directory-managed`
  - control: `a directory-provisioned user who gains a local password reads env_native, and a later directory sync leaves it so`
  - dependent refusal: `set-user-manager refuses a SCIM-provisioned user as a directory-owned identity` — `403`, `PERMISSION_DENIED`, reason `idp_provisioned`, `manager_id` not written (the handler, `runSetUserManager`, driven with the engine the SCIM create wrote to)
  - backfill: `a pre-existing SCIM user is marked, a second pass writes nothing, a password holder and a non-SCIM user are untouched` (first pass `{ directoryProvisioned: 2, marked: 1 }` with one `sys_user` write, second pass `{ 2, 0 }` with zero), and `the backfill pages by subject id and reaches every page` (page size 2 over 3 users).
- `scim-identity-source.test.ts` (new): an absent `sys_scim_subject` table is zero users and no write; any other read failure reaches the caller; a missing-table error naming another relation is not read as the subject table.
- `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts`: the healthy boot reports the backfill count at `info`; a backfill that cannot read is reported at `error` with the refusal in the Error slot.
- `scim-transaction-scope.test.ts` (unchanged) holds the new write to the connection attribution: `(e)` and `(h)` there pin that every write of a SCIM create names the connection.

## Acceptance notes

- ADR-0135 D4 says the row mark has "two writers" (`account.create.after` and the `sys_account` `afterInsert` hook). This PR adds a third, on the SCIM reconcile callback, and the ADR text is not edited here (governed surface). The seat may want a one-line status note on the ADR.
- The SCIM mark fails closed (the SCIM request fails and rolls back) where the two existing writers fail open and log. Inside the vendor's transaction a caught write failure would abort the rest of the transaction on Postgres anyway, so failing the request is the one behaviour that is the same on every driver.
- The `admin/set-user-password` refusal on a cloud-managed environment keys on the same mark; it is not pinned separately here.
